lines.text: Eleven of the twelve lived. The twelfth had been trampled before the gate ever opened. We buried him in our cemetery, under a Greyhollow stone.
You carried me. I felt it. Your hands were freezing.
I'm always cold.
My lens shattered when you touched me. Thirty years, and it never once so much as scratched.
I owe you my life, Lord Lucan. That is an inconvenient thing for a Measurer to owe.
Then don't report me.
I can't. Word has already gone south. And I serve the Order. What I owe the Order is the truth.
But what I owe you, I will pay. I won't name Magister Thorne. As far as my report is concerned, she found nothing, because a junior would find nothing.
In the doorway, Ilse stood very still.
And I will ride south slowly. Very slowly. My arm, you understand.
The next morning, the Measurers saddled their horses. All except one.
Reed. Your horse.
I'm staying, Magister.
I asked eleven times to see my sister. Last night, a farmer carried me out of a stampede on his back. He had three rings. I'm staying.
Take care of her, my lord.
Ten blue robes rode out of the south gate. The smoke festival was over.
I can write the Order's reports, my lord. In the Order's hand, with the Order's codes. Whatever you need them to believe.
Right now, I need them to believe we're harmless.
I think that ship has sailed.
The Lord Who Measured Zero. Chapter 28, coming soon.
